predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: the city of Barcelona, conquered by Louis the Pious of Aquitaine in 801

successors.name: Crown of Aragon
successors.text: the county as it stood in 1162, in personal union with the Kingdom of Aragon

ledger.x: 801: Louis the Pious of Aquitaine conquers Barcelona and the county is established.
878: Wilfred the Hairy becomes count of Barcelona and Girona.
886: Ausona (Osona) is added to Wilfred's counties.
948: Borrell II inherits Urgell from his uncle Sunifred II and holds it with Barcelona, Girona and Ausona.
992: Ramon Borrell succeeds as count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona and Urgell passes to his brother Ermengol.
1112: Ramon Berenguer III marries the heiress of Provence and takes the county.
1117: Cerdanya passes to Ramon Berenguer III.
By 1118: Ramon Berenguer III has captured and rebuilt Tarragona.
1131: Provence goes to the younger son.
July 1148: the siege of Tortosa begins.
30 December 1148: Tortosa surrenders to Ramon Berenguer IV.
30 December 1148: the fighting for Tortosa ends with the surrender.
1149: Lleida, Fraga and Mequinenza fall to Ramon Berenguer IV.
1162: Ramon Berenguer IV dies and Cerdanya goes to his son Pere.
1162: the County of Barcelona enters a personal union with the Kingdom of Aragon.
1162: the county ends as a state of its own.

wars.name: Almanzor's sack of Barcelona (985)
wars.outcome: Barcelona was burned; Borrell II kept the county and, from 988, its effective independence.

wars.name: Almanzor's incursions and the counter-attack on Lleida (1000-1003)
wars.outcome: Ramon Borrell weathered the raids; 'Almanzor died in 1002, and seeing an opportunity Ramon counter-attacked in 1003'.

wars.name: Catalan expedition to Córdoba (1010)
wars.outcome: Ramon Borrell and his brother Ermengol sacked Córdoba in May 1010 and took part in the battle of Aqbat al-Bakr on 2 June 1010 'on the side of the Muslim rebels'; Ermengol died.

wars.name: Expeditions to the Ebro and Segre (1015-1016)
wars.outcome: 'In 1015 and 1016 Ramon made further expeditions to the rivers Ebro and Segre'; the page does not say the campaigns added territory.

wars.name: Almoravid raids on the county (1102)
wars.outcome: Ramon Berenguer III was 'Responding to increased raids into his lands by the Almoravids in 1102'; the page gives no territorial result.

wars.name: Pisan-Catalan expedition to Mallorca and Ibiza (1114-1115)
wars.outcome: 'in 1114 and 1115 attacked with Pisa the then-Muslim islands of Mallorca and Ibiza'; the page records no lasting conquest.

wars.name: Tarragona campaign (1116-1118)
wars.outcome: After the 1116 appeal to Rome 'for a crusade to liberate Tarragona', 'By 1118 he had captured and rebuilt Tarragona'.

wars.name: Siege of Tortosa (1148)
wars.outcome: Christian victory: Tortosa surrendered on 30 December 1148 after a six-month siege; Genoa kept a third of the walled city and sold it to Ramon Berenguer IV in 1153 for 16,000 maravedíes.

wars.name: Conquest of Lleida, Fraga and Mequinenza (1149)
wars.outcome: Lleida capitulated on 24 October (1149); Fraga and Mequinenza fell the same year after a seven-month siege.

certainty.note: Comital frontiers follow castles and rivers; no treaty or survey line is given.
